title: CNCF Ecosystem: Helm, Kustomize & Kubernetes Operators
summary: Standardize application packaging with Helm v3 charts, Kustomize overlays, CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs), and Kubernetes Operators.
learningObjectives: Install, upgrade, list, and roll back production Helm chart releases across namespaces.
Understand the Operator pattern combining CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs) with custom reconciliation controllers.
Manage environment-specific configuration without template sprawl.

curriculumModules.title: Helm v3 Architecture & Release Lifecycle
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Helm v3 is a client-side package manager that renders Go templates with `values.yaml` and stores release state as Secrets inside the target namespace.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Store verified Helm charts as OCI artifacts in a container registry and pin exact chart versions in GitOps manifests.

curriculumModules.title: CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs) & The Operator Pattern
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Operators encode domain-specific operational knowledge (backups, failover, schema migrations) into a Kubernetes controller watching custom API resources.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Use CNCF Operators (CloudNativePG, Strimzi Kafka, Prometheus Operator) to automate Day-2 stateful lifecycle management.

labs.title: Deploying & Upgrading Production Workloads with Helm v3
labs.scenario: Package and deploy the `ingress-gateway` release into the `production` namespace using Helm v3.
labs.productionContext: Helm standardizes third-party and internal microservice releases with atomic upgrades and instant revision rollback.
objectives: Install Helm release `ingress-gateway` using chart `bitnami/nginx` in namespace `production`
Verify the backing `ingress-gateway` Deployment is running in `production`
labs.starterManifest:
# Helm Values Override
replicaCount: 2
image:
  repository: nginx
  tag: 1.27-alpine

steps.title: Install Helm Release in Production
steps.instruction: Run `helm install ingress-gateway bitnami/nginx -n production` to deploy the chart.

steps.title: Verify Helm Release Status
steps.instruction: Run `helm list -n production` to confirm the release status is `deployed`.

validationRules.name: ingress-gateway
validationRules.remediation: Ensure helm install created and reconciled the ingress-gateway deployment.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Run `helm list` to verify the release name is `ingress-gateway` and status is `deployed`.

labs.title: Operator Reconciliation with Custom Resources
labs.scenario: Provision a managed database cluster in `production` by creating a `PostgresInstance` custom resource named `orders-ha-cluster`.
labs.productionContext: Database Operators watch Custom Resources (`PostgresInstance`) and automatically reconcile the underlying StatefulSet, Pods, and ClusterIP Services.
objectives: Verify the operator automatically reconciles Service `orders-ha-cluster-db` in `production`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: database.kubelabs.io/v1alpha1
kind: PostgresInstance
metadata:
  name: orders-ha-cluster
  namespace: production
spec:
  storageGB: 100
  highAvailability: true

steps.title: Verify Operator-Reconciled Database Service
steps.instruction: Check that the Operator created Service `orders-ha-cluster-db` in `production`.

validationRules.description: Operator reconciled Service production/orders-ha-cluster-db with active endpoint
validationRules.name: orders-ha-cluster-db
validationRules.remediation: Ensure PostgresInstance orders-ha-cluster is created in namespace production.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Run `kubectl get postgresinstance -n production` and `kubectl get svc -n production`.

assessmentQuestions.question: Where does Helm v3 store release metadata by default inside a Kubernetes cluster?
options: In a Tiller Pod running inside kube-system
As Kubernetes Secrets in the same namespace where the release is deployed
In a local SQLite file on the worker node
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Helm v3 removed Tiller and stores release history as base64+gzipped Secrets (`sh.helm.release.v1.<name>.v<rev>`) in the release's target namespace.

assessmentQuestions.question: What two components combine to form a Kubernetes Operator?
options: An Ingress resource and a LoadBalancer Service
A CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) and a custom Controller running a reconciliation loop
A Dockerfile and a bash script
assessmentQuestions.explanation: An Operator extends the Kubernetes API via a CRD and pairs it with a custom Controller that watches CRD instances and reconciles external or cluster state.
